run.user_report: Some users see old values after saving, while others see current values.

output.detail: Availability and latency are within baseline.
Availability and latency are within baseline.
Hit rate is 98%, memory is 45%, and network round trips are within baseline.
Primary and read replica are current; replication lag is zero and queries complete normally.

output.log_summary: Affected browsers receive old values from API GET responses after successful saves; no local caching is enabled.
Writes commit to the database and publish invalidations to namespace records-v2. Subsequent reads sometimes return old cache entries.
Read entries are served from records-v1; invalidations arrive on records-v2 and match no entries.

output.description: Cache read namespace reverted to records-v1 during a configuration rollout. API invalidation namespace remains records-v2.

final_diagnosis.explanation: The cache configuration was recently changed to read from namespace records-v1, but API invalidations are still sent to records-v2, causing stale cache reads and inconsistent data visibility for users.

run.user_report: The application intermittently stalls during normal traffic.

output.detail: CPU is 78%; rendering itself remains under 20 ms.
Request handlers wait for a downstream resource; API CPU is normal.
Query CPU is 20%, storage latency is normal, and only 2 connections are active.
Availability and latency are within baseline.

output.log_summary: Handlers spend 2 seconds waiting for database connection acquisition; cache requests finish within baseline.

output.description: API database pool maximum changed from 40 to 2 during the last configuration rollout.

final_diagnosis.explanation: The API is degraded due to handlers waiting for database connection acquisition, despite the database itself being healthy with low active connections. A recent configuration change reduced the API database pool maximum connections from 40 to 2, causing a bottleneck in database connections and leading to intermittent stalls.

run.user_report: Search requests fail after several seconds; other pages work.

output.detail: Availability and latency are within baseline.
Availability and latency are within baseline.
Availability and latency are within baseline.
Cache responds to health probes with normal latency.

output.log_summary: Search requests time out fetching cached search indexes. No database request is issued on the failing path.

output.description: No configuration or deployment changes in the incident window.
Search cache destination changed from cache:6379 to cache:6380. Cache service listens only on 6379.

final_diagnosis.explanation: Search requests fail because the API was recently changed to point to a different cache port (6380) where no cache service is listening, causing timeouts when fetching cached search indexes. Other components are healthy and no cache changes were made, indicating the issue is with the API configuration.

run.user_report: Users see a blank page when opening the application.

output.detail: Page shell loads, but client initialization fails.

output.log_summary: All page loads fail with missing asset app.91.js. The bundle manifest references that file.

output.description: Frontend release replaced the asset directory; app.91.js was omitted from the release artifact.

final_diagnosis.explanation: The frontend is degraded with client initialization failure due to a missing asset app.91.js. The recent frontend deployment replaced the asset directory but omitted this file, causing the blank page issue.
